trickyParts: The spec's starting point (reconcileFailure matching the ERROR alone) cannot work: the ERROR needs RepairGrace (a minute, internal/bus/nats.go:545-551) of stall while reconcileWait is 30 s, so it never fires inside the helper's own wait. The plan's D1 split the helper by what each caller asks for instead; this round implements that.

The repair callback runs on the helper's own polling goroutine, which is the test's goroutine, because testnats.Server.Start, Server.Stop and Cluster.AwaitReady call t.Fatal*, which Go forbids off the test goroutine.

reconcileWait restarts after the repair, so it bounds the reconcile the repair makes possible rather than the repair itself. Measured here: one run in three of testnats.Cluster.AwaitReady spent 15 s on a member no peer heard from before restarting it (nats-server 2.10.29's known start race, internal/testnats/cluster.go:138-145). Without the restart, two such waits inside one 30 s deadline would make the test flaky in the three CI jobs that run cmd/dispatch.
deviations: The plan's Task 1.2 said the ordinary helper's fatal message names the last logged failure; Task 1.5 said reconcileFailure stays the first logged failure and feeds that message. The code reports the first, which is what one scanner gives, and the message says so. The failure repeats with backoff, so the first and the later ones carry the same error.

The plan predicted the new test at about 12 s (the planner measured a 10 s JetStream deadline). Measured here it is 1.6-1.9 s: a three-member cluster with one member stopped refuses a three-copy create at once with `nats: no suitable peers for placement, peer offline` rather than letting the request time out. reconcileWait is unchanged at 30 s.

The simplify pass applied four findings rather than none: logtest.SetDefault in place of the hand-rolled slog swap (the hand-rolled restore left the log package's output pointing at the finished buffer, a defect the old helper already carried in a file this change touches), the connectDispatchStream rename, the two message constants, and splitting the latch from the repair trigger. Both proofs were re-run after it.
openQuestions: The plan's D4 asked the architect whether the operator-facing settings cells must carry the Go identifiers themselves. They do not: each cell states the rule in operator terms and names stall_ms, and the pull request cites reportHookFailure, RepairGrace, hooksDueSince, Client.onReconnect and recoverUntilHealthy by symbol with file and line. Say so if the acceptance means otherwise and the cells get the identifiers.
discoveredComplexity: reportHookFailure is reached from two places (internal/bus/recovery.go:90 and :361), and recoverUntilHealthy has three stop checks, of which only the one after its own attempt (recovery.go:343-349) carries an error. The AGENTS.md sentence names that one and the onReconnect guard, and leaves the two error-less sites (recovery.go:311-313, 363-366) out: they report a stop seen before an attempt, not a failed run.
